narrative.overview: The site is a quiet obsidian vault after hours: deep indigo-black surfaces, one restrained purple accent, and nothing competing for attention. It should feel like opening Obsidian at night — familiar, focused, and trustworthy — because the product promise is local-first privacy. Every design choice defers to that: calm over loud, precise over decorative, restrained over expressive. Density is low and breathing room is generous. The system uses flat tonal layering (successive dark purples) instead of shadows, a single accent used sparingly, and a native system font stack so the page renders instantly with no webfont dependency. Motion is minimal and purposeful — a soft pulse on the thinking indicator, a one-pixel lift on buttons — and always respects reduced-motion.
keyCharacteristics: Dark vault surfaces with one accent, used rarely
Flat tonal layering; shadows only on screenshots and chat panels
Native system type; hierarchy from size and weight only
Refined and restrained components; no decoration for its own sake
Accessible by default: focus rings, skip link, reduced-motion support

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Obsidian Purple is the only chromatic accent. If a screen needs emphasis beyond the accent, use weight, size, or placement — never a second hue.

rules.name: The Tonal Ladder Rule
rules.body: Surfaces step through Vault Night → Vault Soft → Vault Card → Vault Code. Don't introduce a surface outside this ladder.

rules.name: The Native Type Rule
rules.body: No webfonts. If a future display face is ever adopted, it must be a deliberate exception, not a default.

rules.name: The Quiet Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Emphasis is size and weight only — no uppercase labels, no letterspaced kickers, no italic display text.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. The only shadow in the system is Panel Lift, reserved for product captures.

dos: Do keep the accent to one voice per screen — primary CTA, brand mark, or hero phrase, not all three at once.
Do step surfaces through the tonal ladder (Night → Soft → Card → Code) and separate them with 1px Vault Border strokes.
Do let Panel Lift shadow appear only on screenshot frames and the chat mock.
Do use the system stack and size/weight hierarchy; keep prose near 65–75ch.
Do honor reduced-motion (pulse and smooth scroll off) and visible focus rings on every interactive element.
Do use the stroke SVG icon set (1.8px, currentColor, Obsidian Purple Text) for feature icons.
donts: Don't introduce a second accent hue (beyond the semantic Local/Cloud pills and the Warn Amber callout edge).
Don't add shadows to cards, buttons, or nav — flat tonal layering carries depth.
Don't load a webfont or use uppercase letterspaced labels without a deliberate brand exception.
Don't use sharp corners or borderless cards; 14px radius and 1px borders are the form language.
Don't invent testimonials, benchmarks, or evidence — PRODUCT.md forbids fabricating them, and the visual system must not imply them.
Don't use gradient text — emphasis comes from weight, size, or solid accent color.
Don't use emoji or unicode glyphs as icons; draw stroke SVGs instead.
Don't use a thick colored edge (border-left/right above 1px) on callouts or cards; use a full 1px border.
